topic: Bergman's Question 15 on powers in contracted semigroup algebras
title: Examples answering Bergman's Question 15 by extending a partition of von zur Gathen and Roche

creators.name: Wenlin Zhang
creators.affiliation: National University of Singapore; ChronoAI Pte Ltd, Singapore

abstract: We answer Question 15 of George M. Bergman's Thoughts on Eggert's Conjecture, arXiv:1206.0326v2, Section 4, printed page 6, in the negative, including over Q by extending a binomial partition of von zur Gathen and Roche (1997, Table 2, p. 359) to a semigroup. A 59-element commutative semigroup and a 49-element quotient have three generators with distinct nonzero sixth powers but a nonzero linear combination whose sixth power is zero. For these presentations over a characteristic-zero field, the cancellation exists exactly when the field contains a primitive cube root of unity. The construction extends to every positive exponent divisible by six. The older partition yields a 632-element two-generator example at exponent 35 over every characteristic-zero field.
summary: Written proofs give the cyclic 59-element example, 49-element quotient, coefficient-field criterion, multiples-of-six family, 196-element noncommutative example and Question-11 compatibility. A published partition of von zur Gathen and Roche (1997) yields a 632-element rational-field example; the square-zero identity of Almeida et al. (2007) yields strictly noncommutative nilpotent examples of 2n+1 elements for all n>=2. Appendix A gives the different 59-element partition used by the linked Lean declaration, its full cancellation and worked products. Exact finite checks cover all displayed examples and stated instances; the cyclic presentation, quotient and extensions have written proofs.
